JUDGMENT SHEET
IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT
LAHORE
(JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT)
MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN, J.- Appellant,
Muhammad Riaz, has challenged conviction and sentence awarded to
him by the learned Sessions Judge, Khushab, vide judgment dated
28.02.2025, in case FIR No.756 dated 28.09.2023, registered u/s 302
PPC at Police Station City Jauharabad, District Khushab, whereby he
was convicted under Section 302(b) PPC and sentenced to life
imprisonment for committing Qatl-e-Amd of Mst. Samina Shafi. He
was also directed to pay Rs.5,00,000/- as compensation u/s 544-A
Cr.P.C. to the legal heirs of the deceased, in default thereof, to further
undergo six months simple imprisonment. He was also directed to pay
fine of Rs.2,00,000/- to the legal heirs of the deceased, in default
thereof, to further undergo six months simple imprisonment. Benefit
u/s 382-B Cr.P.C. was extended to the convict.
2. Complainant Shan Haider, while setting the machinery of law
in motion through written complaint (Ex-PM), on the basis of which
Cr. Appeal No.17843-J of 2025
Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.
JUDGMENT
body: Date of hearing 12.11.2026 Appellant by: Syed Ali Muhammad Zahid Bukhari and Syed Asjad Abbas Kazmi, Advocates State by: Ms. Noshe Malik, Deputy Prosecutor General.
Complainant by:
M/s Muhammad Irfan Malik and Faseeh Ullah Khan, Advocates.
(Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.)

formal FIR (Ex-PC/1), was drafted later on, narrated facts of the case as under;- “His sister Mst. Samina Shafi, was married with accused Muhammad Riaz, 5/6 years ago and they were residing in Qazi Colony Jauharabad. His sister Mst. Samina Shafi, was issueless and due to this reason accused Muhammad Riaz, used to taunt and torture his sister Mst. Samina. On 27.09.2023, in the evening, he alongwith Muhammad Yousif and Arslan Haider came to the house of accused in Qazi Colony Jauharabad to explain to him that he should not taunt, abuse and torture Mst. Samina and in the night, he alongwith Muhammad Yousif and Arslan Haider slept in the courtyard, whereas Mst. Samina and accused Muhammad Riaz husband-wife, were sleeping in their room on the bed. At night of 28.09.2023, at about 02:00 a.m. we woke up on the screams of Mst. Samina and saw that electricity bulb was glowing in the room and accused Muhammad Riaz, being armed with Churri, gave an instant blow of Churri to Mst. Samina with intention to kill her which hit her on the wrist of left arm. Accused Muhammad Riaz again made a blow of Churri to Mst. Samina with intention to kill her on the left side of her neck. Accused Muhammad Riaz repeated churri blow to Mst. Samina with intention to kill which landed on the right side of her neck. They attempted to rescue Mst. Samina Shafi without caring about their lives and also attempted to catch Muhammad Riaz accused. Accused Muhammad Riaz decamped from the scene while leaving the churri in right side of the neck of Mst. Samina. They attended Mst. Samina Shafi but she succumbed to the injuries at the spot. He alongwith Muhammad Yousif and Arslan Haider witnessed the whole occurrence.

Motive behind the occurrence was that Mst. Samina Shafi was issueless and accused Muhammad Riaz wanted to contract second marriage but Mst. Samina was not allowing him to do so and on this grudge accused Muhammad Riaz committed her murder.” After registration of case, investigation was carried out and on culmination of the investigation, report u/s 173 Cr.P.C. was submitted before the learned trial Court while declaring the appellant as guilty, he was summoned, charge was framed which was denied by him, hence, trial commenced. The prosecution in order to prove its case produced as many as ten PWs. Ocular account in this case was adduced by complainant Shan Haider (PW-8) and Muhammad Yousif (PW-9). Medical evidence was furnished by Dr. Balqees Malik (PW- 5), who conducted autopsy on the dead body of the deceased and investigation of the case was carried out by Imran Khalid SI (PW-10), whereas the remaining witnesses were formal in nature. The prosecution after producing certain documents closed its evidence. After completion of prosecution evidence, statement of the appellant (Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.)

was recorded u/s 342 Cr.P.C., in which he denied the allegation leveled against him. He did not opt to appear as his own witness u/s 340 (2) Cr.P.C., however, produced eight witnesses as DW-1 to DW-8 in his defence. After evaluating prosecution evidence available on record, learned trial Court found the prosecution version correct ‘beyond any shadow of doubt’ which resulted into conviction and sentence of the appellant in the afore stated terms.

3. In support of the instant appeal, learned counsel for the appellant contends that case of the prosecution is inherently flawed, hence, fails to inspire confidence; that the FIR was lodged with an unexplained delay and postmortem examination of the deceased was also conducted with a considerable delay, which creates doubt qua the prosecution case; that the ocular account was furnished by the interested witnesses, whose evidence cannot be relied to maintain conviction of the appellant and even otherwise, they have failed to give plausible explanation qua their presence at the house of the appellant at the time of the occurrence; that there were lot of contradictions in the testimonies of the ocular account; that medical evidence was not in line with the same; that nothing was recovered from possession of the appellant; that motive set up by the prosecution has remained unproved, hence, no corroboratory piece of evidence was available on the record, hence, no implicit reliance can be made on ocular account; that the impugned judgment is based on surmises and conjectures as material evidence available on record in favour of the appellant has been mis-read by the learned trial Court; that the appellant has produced eight witnesses in his defence, whose evidence fully corroborated the defence version of the appellant and lastly prays that since the prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case against the appellant up to hilt, hence, by accepting the instant appeal, he be acquitted of the charge.
4. Conversely, learned Deputy Prosecutor General assisted by learned counsel for the complainant has faithfully defended the (Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.)

impugned judgment by controverting the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and has contended that the prosecution has ably proved its case against the appellant “beyond reasonable shadow of doubt” based on the testimonies of natural witnesses, who had plausibly explained their presence in the house of the appellant at the time of occurrence, thus the same cannot be ignored on any hypotheses; that even otherwise the complainant and other eye witness have no axe to grind against the appellant to involve him in a false murder case that too, real sister of the complainant; that medical evidence was in line with the prosecution case; that sufficient incriminating material was recovered from possession of the appellant; that the prosecution has also produced enough evidence to prove the motive part of the incident, which fully supports the ocular version, so, in presence of voluminous evidence, the appellant does not deserve any leniency and he has rightly been adjudged guilty by the learned trial Court, hence, the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed.

5. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant, learned Law Officer assisted by learned counsel for the complainant and perused the record with their assistance and noticed that at least three prosecution witnesses of ocular account including complainant Shan Haider (PW-8), claimed that they had witnessed the incident, wherein appellant, Muhammad Riaz, had murdered his wife, Mst. Samina Shafi (deceased), by inflicting multiple knife (چھری) blows on her person. All these three witnesses claimed that they stayed in the house of the appellant, over night as there was some previous quarrel between husband and wife, as they were not having any issue despite the fact that they got married 5/6 years prior to the incident and the appellant wanted to remarry but his wife Mst. Samina Shafi, was not giving him such permission. Complainant Shan Haider and his uncle Muhammad Yousif appeared in the dock as PW-8 & PW-9 respectively, whereas another witness of ocular account, Arslan (Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.)

Haider, stayed away, resultantly, he was given up by the prosecution being unnecessary. Having analyzed the evidence and facts of the case with the assistance of learned counsel for the parties, I believe that the ocular account does not fit in the manner in which, the deceased was done to death. Firstly, as per prosecution case, the witnesses three in number, whereas the appellant was all alone and as per version of the eye witnesses, when they heard hue and cry of Mst. Samina Bibi, they attracted to the room, where both husband and wife, were sleeping and in their view, appellant Muhammad Riaz, inflicted multiple blows on her body but this story narrated by these PWs is hard to believe as they neither tried to save the deceased from the alleged assault of the appellant nor could apprehend him. Had they been available at the crime scene, it was very easy for three persons to apprehend one assailant as he was not carrying any firearm weapon; secondly, as per contents of the FIR, the incident took place at 02:00 a.m. (night) on 28.09.2023, whereas same was reported to the police with a noticeable delay of about eight hours and fourty five minutes at 10:45 a.m. and on going through postmortem examination report (Ex-PG), it is noticed that the same was conducted at 03:10 p.m. with the delay of thirteen hours and ten minutes. This delay in lodging the FIR and in conducting postmortem examination, remained unexplained on part of the prosecution. Even Imran Khalid SI (PW-10), Investigating Officer of the case had stated that the police had reached at the crime scene at 08:30 a.m., however, fact remained that statement (Ex-PM) of complainant Shan Haider (PW-8), on the basis of which formal FIR (Ex-PC/1) was later on, drafted, was got written by the said police officer at 10:30 a.m. So, this long delay speaks volume about the truthfulness and sanctity of the prosecution version qua presence of the PWs and having witnessed the occurrence. There is hardly any cavil with the proposition that the delay and deliberation always dilute the FIR on its evidentiary foundation as held by the apex Court of the (Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.)
country in cases of “MEHMOOD AHMAD”
and “IFTIKHAR HUSSAIN and others”

6. During course of investigation, it came on the record that in fact, appellant Muhammad Riaz, made call to Rescue 1122 and also to the Incharge Helpline (15). In response to that, firstly three officials of Rescue 1122 i.e. Hafiz Abdul Rasheed, District Emergency Officer, Muhammad Nadeem, Emergency Medical Technician and Tasleem Arif Khan, Junior Computer Operator, reached at the crime scene and they while appearing in the dock before the learned trial Court as DW- 1, DW-2 and DW-3 respectively, have candidly admitted that it was, appellant Muhammad Riaz, who made call and in response to that call, they reached at the place of occurrence on vehicle No.KBA-12, round about 07 O’ Clock and they found that the door of room was bolted from inside and after breaking the exhaust whole (روشن دان), the door was opened with the help of a child and after entering the said room, dead body of Mst. Samina Shafi, was found lying, who had committed suicide with knife (چھری). Similarly, Usman Manzoor, Police Communication Officer/In-Charge Rescue-15, District Police Officer, Khushab at Jauharabad, while appearing in the dock as DW- 4, had deposed that on 28.09.2023, he was working as In-Charge Rescue-15 at DPO Office Khushab at Jauharabad, on the same day at 07:41 a.m., he received call through mobile No.0341-1321122 regarding the suicide of female, Mst. Samina wife of the appellant, aged about 34/35 years. He passed the said call to Control Pukar-15 and then, one Muhammad Usman, Sales and Details Officer, U-fone Cellular Company, while appearing in the dock as DW-6, confirmed that the above said sim number from which the police received phone call, was registered in the name of the appellant, who was using the same. The defence has also adduced Daniyal Ahmad, aged about 10 years as DW-8, who verified that on 28.09.2023 at about 07:00 a.m., on asking of officials of Rescue-1122, he entered the room, through MEHMOOD AHMAD and 3 others v. THE STATE and another (1995 SCMR 127) IFTIKHAR HUSSAIN and others v. THE STATE (2004 SCMR 1185) (Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.)

exhaust (روشن ڈان) and opened the hook of the door from inside the room. Learned counsel for the complainant, while referring a recent judgment passed by the august Supreme Court of Pakistan in case titled “Waris Masih”

, argued that since murder was done inside house of the appellant, so, he was burdened to prove that in which circumstances, the deceased was done to death. Paragraph No.7 of the said judgment reads as under;- “It is worth mentioning that where a wife is found dead inside the matrimonial home, the first and foundational question for determination is the nature of the death, namely, whether it was natural or unnatural. Once the prosecution succeeds in establishing that the death was unnatural, the next question is whether the death was the result of suicide or homicide. Upon a finding that the death was homicide in nature, the focus of investigation necessarily turns to the circumstances surrounding the occurrence, particularly the place of occurrence. At this juncture, it becomes necessary to distinguish between the concepts of burden of proof and onus of proof, which though related, operate in distinct legal spheres. The burden of proof refers to the obligation to establish the entire case and the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, a burden which, in criminal proceedings, always rests upon the prosecution and never shifts. The onus of proof, on the other hand, pertains to the responsibility of proving a particular fact or issue, which may, depending upon the circumstances of the case, shift during the course of trial.” On going through the above excerpt from the esteemed judgment, I have noticed that the Apex Court has laid down two conditions, first that the prosecution has to establish that death of the deceased was unnatural, thus whether it was suicide or homicide. And once, it was found that the same was homicide in nature, then focus of the investigation necessarily turns to the circumstances surrounding the occurrence, particularly the place of occurrence and though the burden of proving the charge against the appellant remains upon the prosecution as it never shifts, however, the onus of proof, on the other hand, pertains to the responsibility of proving a particular fact or issue, may depending upon the circumstances of the case, shifts during the course of trial. However, I feel that the facts and circumstances of case in hand, are totally different from that of the Waris Masih v. The State in Jail Petition No.787/2018 (Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.)

case referred supra as in that case nobody had claimed that they were the witnesses of the incident including Jangi Masih, father of Mst. Jamila Bibi/deceased, complainant of said case, rather injured daughter of the deceased lady, appeared in the dock as one of the prosecution witnesses.

7. But in the instant case, at least three prosecution witnesses claimed their availability at the crime scene but they absolutely remained failed to substantiate their stance on account of reasons discussed supra and when case of the prosecution and defence is seen in juxta position, the stance taken by the appellant seems to be reasonable and more plausible as the defence has proved in meticulous terms by adducing independent witnesses like officials of Rescue-1122 as DW-1 to DW-3, Police Communication Officer Incharge Rescue-15 as DW-4, they verified that they attended the crime scene in response of telephonic call made by appellant, Muhammad Riaz and minor child, Daniyal Ahmad, who also deposed in clear and unambiguous terms that he entered in room of the deceased, which was bolted from inside, through exhaust whole (روشن دان) and unbolted the door from inside. Whereas veracity of the prosecution witnesses is seriously doubtful because of long delay in lodging the FIR and conducting postmortem examination of the deceased. Had they been available at the crime scene, there was no impediment for lodging the FIR within time as the Police Station was situated at a distance of just two kilometers away from the crime scene. So in that eventuality, I believe that defence had convincingly dislodged the prosecution evidence, and remained successful to prove that the death of the deceased was though unnatural but result of suicide.

8. So, while fortifying the ratio decidendi settled by the august Supreme Court of Pakistan in supra case of “Waris Masih” the impugned judgment, whereby the appellant was convicted and sentence cannot be allowed to stand, I, therefore, allow this appeal, set (Muhammad Riaz v. The State, etc.)
aside the same and appellant, Muhammad Riaz is acquitted of the charge. He is in jail, be released forthwith, if not required to be detained in any other case.
(MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN)
JUDGE APPROVED FOR REPORTING JUDGE Sajid
